Question Choices: For sqrt(x^2)/x what expression replaces sqrt(x^2)?
Hints: The principal square root is nonnegative.|Squaring loses the sign of x.
Solution: For real x, sqrt(x^2)=abs(x), the nonnegative magnitude. It equals x for x>=0 and -x for x<0. Replacing it with x for all real inputs would be incorrect. sqrt(x^2)=|x|.

Hints: Replace sqrt(x^2) with |x|.|For negative x the absolute value is -x.
Solution: For a negative-infinity limit, x is eventually negative. Thus sqrt(x^2)=abs(x)=-x. Substitute that sign-correct identity before simplifying; the sign of the denominator still matters. lim x->-oo of Abs(x)/x = -1
